newsitem.title: USA: Fort Howard expanding plant, adding 100 workes.
newsitem.headline: Fort Howard expanding plant, adding 100 workes.

text.p: Fort Howard Corp. said Wednesday that it will spend $160 million to expand one of its mills and add about 100 employees to increase tissue paper production in response to growing demand for its products.
The company, whose consumer brands include Mardi Gras napkins and paper towels, said it will add production capacity at one of its mills either in Rincon, Ga., near Savannah, or in Muskogee, Okla.
It said the decision on which plant to expand would be based on access to markets, available labour, environmental considerations and other factors.

"Our dramatic gains in the at-home consumer market for both private-label and branded products, as well as our successful new product introductions for the away-from-home market, have set the stage for our growth," company President Michael Riordan said in a statement.
Fort Howard said its share of the at-home tissue products market has grown from about 4 percent in 1985 to over 11 percent in 1996.
The company, which is based in Green Bay. Wis., said the plant expansion, which will include installation of a state-of-the-art 270-inch paper processing machine, is expected to be completed in 1999.
Fort Howard already owns eight of the 11 modern 270-inch paper machines operating in the world.
"Newer and larger paper machines provide enormous efficiencies. No company can compare to us in that category," Riordan said.
Fort Howard's stock added 12.5 cents to $23.625 in late morning trading on the Nasdaq market.
